sections.value:
**Performance: pass-with-notes** at `a63edce13234182c8ca22c65500a2b6270337b8f`.

Delta review since `88509c3a80e6fa919ee3c5c75f0804e5d4402d67`: main merge `7cdda03`, fixes `283d774`, formatter-only `642e64b`, and test-only `a63edce`. The updated final packet supersedes the missing-worktree/old-head blocker. Main's inherited features are not independently re-reviewed; the earlier performance verdict otherwise stands.

| Surface | Cost delta |
|---|---|
| Literal tmux names | `tmux/src/lib.rs:1486-1493,1536-1555` applies `name.replace('#', "##")` at rename and new-window name boundaries. One linear scan and owned string per name; resulting bytes are original bytes plus the number of hashes, at most twice the input size. Existing argv construction then copies that value. No extra tmux command, discovery, process check or timer. This prevents implicit format/job interpretation instead of adding another process producer. |
| Existing rename launch | Release/assign behavior remains conditional as previously reviewed: an eligible rename still pays the existing recorded tmux launch. “No new launch site” does not mean releases/assigns launch nothing. New-window retains its existing invocation too. |
| Printed guidance | `delivery/role_send.rs` now constructs stored-role/instance/seat/project guidance through `picture::command`. Quoting/escaping cost and allocation scale with argument bytes; resulting lines are not executed. Quoted placeholders alter presentation, not retry scheduling, reads, withdrawal transactions or fanout. |
| Main convergence | The combined merge retains plan 212's drained receipt alongside main's batch-history receipt changes. The assignment hook is still awaited after the writer has returned (`community/directory.rs:943-947`), then the existing rename follows. No second drain or new autonomous loop is introduced. Prior unpaged queue, sequential batch-hook and assign-response latency limits remain. |
| Final two commits | `642e64b` only rewraps the expected-verb array in a TS test. `a63edce` adds the `/bin/sh printf` hostile-instance round-trip to the existing regression test. Those shell/file checks are test work, not production commands or cost. |

**CI proof:** GitHub is CLEAN at this exact final head. [CI 42370745800](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42370745800) has all four jobs successful, and latest [delivers 42371056530](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42371056530) succeeds. Rust JUnit records **2,067 executed cases, zero failures/errors**; five Rust tests were skipped separately. The literal new-window argv unit, hostile-instance `/bin/sh` round-trip, tmux rename adapter case and all six spawn guards are listed as passed.

The rename adapter case's recorded duration is 0.350 s and its source includes a 300 ms marker check; its fixture can return early if tmux is unavailable. This review does not certify the runner's exact tmux version or reproduce the real-tmux test locally. Herring owns the complete format/security closure.

No local builds, tests, mutation runs, runtime probes, actual sends/assigns/releases or review-tree changes. Prior request-list body/candidate-work limits, closed-history retention, awaited drain latency and later #135 gate-composition limits are not discharged by this string-only repair.

**Migration policy:** 0037 is above current main's 36. If #152's 0038 or #153's 0039 lands first, #149 must receive a higher migration number on rebase under the prime's merge-order rule; keeping only a higher schema pragma is not that renumbering.

**Still owed:** matched live deployment launch-rate and CPU/RSS receipts with PID/build, elapsed time and workload; contended assign/drain/rename latency remains unmeasured.
